questions.question: Where should a hazardous material's identification number appear?

options.text: On a sticker near the shipping container.

questions.explanation: The ID number must appear on the packaging and shipping papers. It must also appear on cargo tanks and other bulk packaging.

questions.question: What should you NOT use when loading hazardous materials containers?
questions.explanation: Never use hooks or other equipment that could damage containers. Always protect hazardous materials containers during loading.

questions.question: Shippers package hazardous materials in order to ____ them.
questions.explanation: Shippers package hazardous materials to keep them completely contained. Vehicles must display placards to show the cargo risk.

questions.question: What must you do when transporting chlorine and approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
You must slow down before crossing the tracks.
You can cross if no warning lights are flashing.
You can cross if no other vehicles are in sight.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: When transporting any amount of chlorine, you must always stop at a railroad crossing 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track.

questions.question: When must a driver take the HazMat knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You must pass the HazMat knowledge test and pass a federal background check before every CDL renewal.

questions.question: What should you do before opening trailer doors during a fire?

options.text: Check if the doors are hot.
Find someone else to open them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if the doors are hot.
questions.explanation: Feel the doors first to check if they are hot. If they are, there may be a cargo fire inside. Keep the doors closed because opening them could make the fire worse by adding oxygen.

questions.question: How should hazardous materials placards be used on a vehicle?

options.text: They should be on all four sides of the vehicle.
They should be used only by Class A licensed drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be on all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle when required.

questions.question: What must a package with liquid containers display?

options.text: Arrows pointing the correct upright direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows pointing the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Packages with liquid containers must display arrows pointing the correct upright direction. Place these packages facing the correct direction.

questions.question: Who must identify the hazard class of a hazardous material?
questions.explanation: The shipper must determine the ID number, proper shipping name, hazard class, and packing group. The shipper also determines correct packaging, labels, markings, and placards.

questions.question: What is a clue that your shipment contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipper deals in fireworks or munitions.
Your last shipment was labeled as hazardous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper deals in fireworks or munitions.
questions.explanation: A clue that a shipment may contain hazardous materials is the shipper's business type. Examples include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, pest control businesses, agricultural suppliers, and explosives or fireworks dealers.

questions.question: To drive a vehicle that carries hazardous materials, you must have:

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a passenger endorsement.
A CDL with an air brake endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials, even if it is not carrying them at that moment.

questions.question: Who must put placards on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: The shipper provides the placards, but the driver must actually place them on the vehicle.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: Open the liquid discharge valves when loading or unloading. Keep them closed at all other times.

questions.question: Hazardous materials containers must be:

options.text: Secured to prevent movement during transport.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured to prevent movement during transport.
questions.explanation: Secure containers so they will not fall, slide, or bounce during transport. All hazardous materials packages must be secured.

questions.question: What does a driver need to accept a hazardous materials package, unless it looks unsafe?
questions.explanation: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they certify it was done correctly. You may accept the shipper's certification unless the package looks unsafe or does not follow regulations.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, your vehicle should not be parked:
questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Also never park it within five feet of the road.

questions.question: If a box contains liquid containers, it must have:

options.text: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.
The number of containers listed on it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Boxes with liquid containers must have arrows that point in the correct upright direction.

questions.question: If cargo is leaking, you should:

options.text: Touch the leaking material to identify it.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify it.
Spray the leaking containers with water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify it.
questions.explanation: If you find a leak, use the shipping papers and labels to identify the material. Do not touch the leaking material.

questions.question: If your vehicle with explosives breaks down, you should warn other drivers with:

options.text: Your arms waving from the roadway.

questions.explanation: Use reflective triangles or red lights to warn other drivers. Never use burning signals like flares when transporting explosives.

questions.question: Hazardous materials may be transported by:

options.text: A driver with a CDL and hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver with a CDL and hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials.

questions.question: The correct way to check tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tires with your hand.

questions.explanation: Check each tire at the start of every trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only way to check tire pressure correctly.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials is by:
questions.explanation: The manual has information needed to pass the written exam for a hazardous materials endorsement, but it does not cover everything needed to do the job safely. Training courses teach you more.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in a trailer, it should be:

options.text: Left to air dry without washing.

questions.explanation: Areas exposed to corrosive liquids must be washed thoroughly with water.

questions.question: A person watching a placarded vehicle must be:

options.text: Inside a gas station looking out through a window.
In the vehicle, awake or asleep.

questions.explanation: A person watching a placarded vehicle must be awake inside the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. They must know the hazards of the materials, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the vehicle if needed.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with empty hazardous materials cargo tanks, a driver:

options.text: Must slow down at railroad crossings but does not have to stop.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle has cargo tanks used to carry hazardous materials, you must stop before crossing railroad tracks. This rule applies whether the tanks are full or empty.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves on compressed gas tanks closed. The only exception is during loading and unloading.

questions.question: If you see hazardous materials leaking while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep driving to find a phone and call the National Response Center.
Leave the area to find help.

questions.explanation: If you discover hazardous materials leaking, park the vehicle as soon as possible. Continuing to drive increases the contamination trail, creating more danger and higher cleanup costs.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, a driver needs:

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a tank endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: To drive any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials, you must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: What does a hazardous materials shipping paper describe?

options.text: How the materials will be transported
Who should accept the materials being transported

questions.explanation: A shipping paper describes the hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all types of shipping papers.

questions.question: If a product requires a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard, when must you use it?

options.text: When transporting the product in a non-sealed container.

questions.explanation: For applicable materials, you must always display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard and the correct hazard class placard, even for small amounts.
